messages.content:
Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Dev: does that mean we can reset the breaker with the heater off? asking before anybody tries it. The cooler is still on battery, and I’m fine leaving it that way until we get an answer from the office.

Mara: no, not yet. Nia said to leave it tripped until staff can inspect the post. If they say the post is safe to use, we can ask whether a reset is appropriate; we shouldn’t assume the neighbor’s working socket settles it.

Lee: that’s clear. I’ve put a note on the van dash with the time it tripped and what was plugged in. It was about 6:10, heater on low, cooler cycling, kettle recently used, and no lights or other loads added.

Dev: we can still make breakfast on the camp stove outside, with the kettle off the power setup. I’ll keep it on the cleared gravel pad and away from the tent fabric. The food is in the cooler, so no need to open it much.

Mara: thanks. please don’t run the stove under the awning if the showers start. The forecast has rain later, but it’s calm at the moment. We’ve got the picnic shelter as a dry place to eat if we need it.

Nia (office): quick update, Pat is on the way from the north loop with a meter and a replacement weather cover. Please keep the post breaker as it is and leave the connector disconnected. Pat will check the receptacle before advising you.

Mara: got it. we’ll leave the switch untouched and keep the plug disconnected. The cracked flap is on the post-side inlet cover, not on the van cord. I’ll show Pat the photo and the note with the trip time.

Dev: the rain has started lightly, so I moved the dry cord end back inside the van and shut the inlet cover as much as it will close. The cord isn’t connected at either end now, and the walkway is clear.

Lee: Pat arrived at 7:42 and looked at the post before asking us to plug anything back in. He said he’ll test the receptacle and the breaker first, then check our cord and van inlet. We’re staying out of his work area.

Mara: Pat says if the breaker stays tripped after he tests the post with our cord disconnected, we should not reset it or use that post; he’ll mark it out of service and tell the office. If it holds during his test, he’ll check the van cord and inlet before telling us whether we can connect again.

Pat (staff): for now, leave the heater unplugged either way. If the connection is cleared for use, use only the cooler and lights tonight, and call the office if the breaker trips again. If the post is marked out of service, don’t use a neighboring site’s outlet; I’ll ask the office about the unpowered overflow pad.

Mara: understood. if the post is out of service, we’ll take the van to the overflow pad only if the office confirms there’s room; otherwise we’ll stay parked and keep the cooler on its battery. We’ll wait for Pat’s check before deciding.

Dev: the office also confirmed that, if we end up on the overflow pad, we can keep our reservation through Sunday and use the washroom block by the gate. They haven’t assigned us a different spot, so we shouldn’t move until they do.

Lee: last note for the thread, Pat is still testing the post and hasn’t given us a result yet.
